Barranquilla: What to Do About Slow and Congested Mobility, According to TomTom Traffic Index

2026-09-14 Zona Cero TomTom Traffic Index, Barranquilla, Colombia, traffic congestion, urban mobility, travel times, city planning
Read the source article

Quick summary

Barranquilla ranked as one of the world's slowest and most congested cities in the TomTom Traffic Index 2025, with a 10km trip taking over 36 minutes on average and 46 minutes during evening rush hour, prompting experts to propose solutions from better public transit to parking pricing.

Key takeaways

  • Barranquilla ranked #1 as the slowest city and #19 for congestion globally in the TomTom Traffic Index 2025
  • A 10km trip took 36 minutes 35 seconds on average, rising to 46 minutes 9 seconds during evening rush hour
  • Congestion increased 1.7 percentage points from 61.1% to 62.8% in 2025
  • Barranquilla ranked as the 4th most congested city in Colombia, after Bogotá, Medellín, and Cali
  • Expert Isidro Ruiz disputes the global ranking, calling congestion "localized" rather than city-wide
  • Road works, canalization, and intersection improvements contribute to temporary congestion
  • Proposed solutions include strengthening public transit, limiting building heights, and implementing parking fees in tourist areas
